The harbor opens at six in the morning. Fishermen unload their catch while buyers walk between the crates, checking the ice and pressing thumbs against gills. By eight the best fish are gone, and the gulls work what is left.

Prices depend on the weather more than on demand. A calm week means small catches and higher prices; a storm keeps the boats in port entirely. The harbor master keeps a chalkboard with the day's rates, and nobody argues with the numbers on it.

Old Marta runs the scale at the end of the dock. She has done this for thirty years. When someone questions a reading, she lifts the fish again without a word, and the second number always matches the first.
